title: Apple Expo Paris 2004
speaker: Steve Jobs
content:
I don't know how I top that.
I should just walk back off stage and say thank you very much and good night.

That's an awesome, awesome welcome.
Thank you.
And uh to everyone watching here and and there'll be a lot of people who get to watch this later on today on the internet, um there could not be a better place to have a show than Paris at the end of summer.
I mean it's a gorgeous day out there in the city.
It's an incredible time and and Apple Expo this year looks to be a huge hit yet again.
We have more vendors than we did last year exhibiting at the show and a big jump up even more in attendance with people pre-registering to be here at the show.
So Apple Expo is going to be amazing and and for all those who watch on the internet who who can't be here, we can only say we wish you were here, but we're really glad we're here.
It's incredible in Paris.
Yes.

Oh, before we begin, I would like to pass on some words from Steve.
As you know, uh Steve loves coming to Paris and wishes he could be here.
And he asked me to pass along that while he can't be here, I think you all know, he's at home recuperating from his successful surgery.
And many of us have had a chance to meet with him and and check up on him and he's doing great.
And he's and he's really, really coming along well and and as you know, he'll be back at work in September.
September can't come soon enough.
Yes.

So I know, I I know I speak for all of us here that we really look forward to Steve coming back to Apple this September.
So let's get started with our show.
I'm going to start by first talking about our music products.
I think you know a few of them.
You've probably heard about the iPod by now.
Yep, the iPod comes in two amazing models now.
The iPod Mini, it's 5 gigabyte hard drive and five really fun colors and the all new fourth generation white iPod.
This new iPod has been a huge hit.
It's a great new design.
It integrates the click wheel from the iPod Mini into the white iPod and it has a lot of great new features like my favorite, the shuffle songs menu right in the top level of the menu.
So with one click, you get access to all your music library randomly.
So as you're running along the beach or biking, you can have access to everything on your on your iPod.
And it's hard to believe, but this new iPod design is even slightly thinner than the previous models.
Yet it still holds its 20 and 40 gigabyte hard drives and 5 to 10,000 songs.
And more importantly, it's increased battery life, 50% more battery life to 12 hours.
So this great new iPod and the successful iPod Mini continues the great success story that is iPod.
For example, the market share of the iPod is measured in the US by NPD has gone up again, 58%.
Now this is the market share of all MP3 players.
That's both flash based and hard drive based.
And so while we know there are a lot of music players in the market, more and more customers choose the iPod.
And we all know why that is, right?
Because it's the best music player in the market.
And Apple's innovation really shows in this great product.
Well we're starting, what we hope is the beginning of yet another great holiday season.
We hope a lot of people find iPods under their Christmas tree.
We're going to start the marketing off with a bang by coming out with yet another version of our great silhouette TV ad.
So what I'd like to do is show you the brand new silhouette TV ad that just started running this weekend, first on MTV.
Let's run that new ad.

Yeah, isn't that cool?

There it is from the side.
Again from the front.
It's a little it's very small.
The slide really looks it's probably about 25 feet big on that slide, but in real life it's smaller than that and it gives incredible dynamic range and base response.
So there's just so many good options for customers now.
The millions and millions of iPod customers can choose from over 250 third party products that work with the iPod and it's a great healthy ecosystem of products growing around the iPod to help us get music around our homes and around our lives.
Well at Apple, we've also been working on some very innovative products to help you get music around your home.
And recently we introduced Airport Express.
And it's starting to get out there and people are realizing what a cool product this is.
Well first of all, it's a base station, just like the Airport base station before it.
And if you want to get wireless internet in your home to get onto broadband via cable or DSL or satellite, this is a great base station to do that.
You just plug it in and now you have wireless access in your house.
Even cooler, it's so small that you can just throw it in your bag and take it with you.
So when you're traveling around the world like many of us do, you plug it in at your hotel room and now you have wireless access in your hotel room as well.
And if you want to extend the airport network in your house, this also works automatically with that.
You can have a base station already in your home, you add a second Airport Express and now you have a wider coverage throughout your home.
So it's a great base station in many ways, but the really cool thing is what it does with music.
It has a stereo jack on the bottom of it.
You plug in your stereo system, analog or digital optical stereo.
And now around your house, you have a wireless network for music.
This is a pretty big breakthrough.
So imagine you have a Mac in your bedroom and you want to stream music to a stereo in your kitchen, just put an Airport Express there and do that.
Or perhaps you have a PC.
Yes, some people do have PCs.
And we need to get music out of them as well, out of iTunes, and you can stream perhaps to your stereo in your living room.
So it really is the first successful wireless network for music in your home.
And it's so easy to use, which is what you'd expect from Apple.
It integrates completely with our great iTunes music software.
When you plug in speakers into your Airport Express, a menu automatically shows up in iTunes that lets you access all those speaker systems you set up.
And you just pull down to where you want the music to go.
You select perhaps your living room, your home theater setup or wherever your speakers are and the music now gets sent there wirelessly from iTunes.
So that integration of software and hardware that Apple is renowned for is just a tremendous simple solution for our customers with Airport Express and iTunes.
So that's the new Airport Express and it's one of the coolest ways to get music around your home and in your life.
Well the other area I mentioned was the car.
We're just at the beginning of a a really big revolution of integrating the iPod with cars and who better to start that with than with BMW.
BMW is a great company that also understands innovative products and we've been working with them on the first true seamless integration of the iPod and an automobile.
So for example, today what you would have to do in your car to get music through your your car stereo and a lot of us all do this is we for example buy a cassette adapter and you plug it into the headphone jack of your iPod.
Then you get an AC adapter that plugs into your cigarette lighter and plug that in to keep charging your iPod and now you have music wherever you go.
It's not the ideal driving experience, but it's music at least in your car.
Well, what we really want is for it to look like this.
And that's what you can do with the iPod adapter from BMW.
You can use the iPod in your car and yet have the gorgeous environment you want.
So where is the iPod?
Well, it's in the glove box.
There's a single cable there that plugs right into the connector on the bottom of the iPod and over that connector you get great quality stereo audio, you get power charging your iPod.
It's even smart enough to deactivate the buttons on the iPod so nothing in your glove box accidentally bumps it and changes your music when you don't want it to.
Just close up your glove box and you get driving.
So maybe you're racing down the Autobahn at 200 kilometers per hour, blowing somebody by and you want to crank up the tunes, you can do it right on your steering wheel.
Sounds like fun to me.
Of course, you can also control it from the stereo head unit in your car.
It uses the same interface as you're used to with a CD player, but instead of controlling CDs, you're now controlling your playlist up to six playlists on your iPod and those songs on that playlist.
That's just a little bit about the things we're doing to not only make great iPods, but to make digital music part of our life all around our house.
So you can get access to your music wherever you are and in your car while you're driving.
Now BMW is actually here at Apple Expo.
They have cars at the show so you can check it out.
And they'll be talking about how you can now be able to get uh support in your BMW in Europe this fall with BMW authorized service centers.
So it's starting to come to Europe as well.
Let's talk about the music store.
Along with having a great jukebox and a great iPod, what's really brought this all together and made sense for all of us is the ability to finally legally buy music on the internet through the iTunes Music Store, the first successful music store.
Well, as you know, we started this in the US.
In the US, we've built a library of over a million songs that customers can purchase and download.
And recently this summer, we we announced that we've passed the 100 million song mark for songs sold.
Something never done before, a major milestone.
Yes.

So certainly congratulations goes to the iTunes team, iTunes Music Store team.
You don't know how hard they work day and night getting great music and great services to everybody.
This doesn't come easy and they work so hard to be as successful as they are.
And and it shows in our market share.
We're not the only music store that customers can buy music from, but we're the best music store and that's why so many people choose to buy music on iTunes because we work hardest and deliver the best music experience.
Well, based on customer demand, of course, we had to bring it to Europe.
Customers over here really asked us to bring the iTunes Music Store and we started this year.
We started first in the UK, France and Germany.
And as you know, we've built a library in Europe over over 700,000 songs and we're investing a lot in that and growing it every day.
We have a lot of great music from the five majors as well as increasingly from dozens and dozens of independent music companies.
Great bands like with exclusive content like Bon, Rune 5 and and Schiller.
Yeah.
Yeah, great band.
Well, I'm sure I'm sure you've heard some of the results of that.
In the first week, we sold over 800,000 songs in those three countries.
And that was a big accomplishment.
That was 16 times the closest competitor.
As I said, there were already music stores in Europe, none as great as the iTunes Music Store.
So how have we done since then?
You might be wondering.
It's been 10 weeks since we introduced that music store in the UK, France and Germany.
And in that time, I'm happy to announce we've sold 5 million songs.

So what are our plans with the music store in Europe?
Well, to bring it to more and more of our European customers as more and more people want access to this great technology.
We started in the US, we brought it to the UK, France and Germany and our next stop is to bring it in October across the EU countries with an English store accessible by more and more countries.
So we're going to continue to bring the iTunes Music Store across Europe and allow it to grow by just meeting the needs of all the customers who want it so badly.
So that's an update on our music products on the iPod and the iTunes Music Store and what a great success they are.
We continue to work hard and innovate in the space like no one else.
I now talk about the Mac.
MacOS 10, the current release Panther has been the best release we've ever had of MacOS, both in units sold as well as the number of customers now using MacOS 10.
And really the transition is over.
The majority of our customers all use MacOS 10.
The majority of our developers are now delivering only MacOS 10 software and there are great software applications available.
Over 12,000 native applications and growing every day on MacOS 10.
And as you go through the show here in Paris at Apple Expo, you're going to see more and more new products that are available and being announced here at the show.
Just to name a few of them, Quark is delivering Quark Express.

Hold on, my button's having some fun.
We don't make these clickers.
We're having fun with slides.
There we go.
Quark Express is showing off Quark's QPS system running on Xserves.
Uh 4D, that great database created over here in Europe has the new 2004 version.
Alias is showing their new high-end Maya Unlimited running on MacOS 10.
Lego has worked with Feral Interactive to deliver a brand new Bionicle game on the Mac as well as other gaming platforms.
Vara is bringing the new Video Q software, which is great multimedia presentation software on MacOS 10.
And Hachette Multimedia is a French encyclopedia and those are just a few examples of all the great software that you're going to find here at Apple Expo and the tremendous momentum on MacOS 10 from our developers.
I'd like to show you two products specifically because they're so much fun and give you a sense of the great things happening on MacOS 10.
First, THQ, they're a game developer working with a really major fun movie studio who's launching a new movie and they have a killer game coming out on the Mac tying in with that movie.
I'd like to introduce Shiraz Akmal.
He's the director of development for THQ.
Shiraz?

shared between Mac and Windows clients. And to be able to create richer emails using standard HTML composition for sharing with Windows customers. And a lot of little attention to detail like you may not realize it that the the built-in word processor in Mac OS 10 text edit has the ability already to open word files. Well, now with Tiger, we've added support for word files that have tables included in them. So many touches to make the integration in the Windows world easier for Mac OS 10 customer.

But Mac OS 10 isn't just about fitting in. It's about standing out with innovative new features. And both we and Microsoft are talking about the next great thing in an operating system, and that's search. Search is the next big revolution in personal computer operating systems. And again, we know where we're going in Mac OS 10 and Tiger. We have a clear vision. Um, it seems like there's some turmoil on the other side of where they're going. And so again, no need to to tease them here for their for their problems. Uh, they they can't figure it out, but what we have is an amazing solution.

And so why do we care? Well, it used to be really easy. You would create a folder, you put a file in it, and you know where it is. But more and more with these 20 and 30 and 40 gigabyte systems with thousands and thousands of files, it's becoming harder and harder to find our documents on our system. A lot of people joke or complain that it's actually easier to go into Google and search the internet for a site out of a billion sites and find it in a second than it is to find something in your own hard drive. Right? Well, we've got to solve that. That's not okay.

So we've been hard at work at the technology to solve that problem. The easier thing was figuring out how to create an underlying system that can find something really fast. The hard thing was to figure out how to make that easy to use. And as we thought about it and worked on it, it became apparent to us that we already had an answer. We solved this in iTunes. In iTunes, we created a system where you can have thousands and thousands of songs, but you just start to type in a few letters of what you want and instantly you find it. And it doesn't matter what you're typing in, an artist name, a song title, the name of an album, a genre. You just start typing and iTunes finds what you want in a split second. The more you type, the more refined your search. That's how search should work in a personal computer.

So that's what we set out to do, to build that kind of technology in at the system level and help your entire personal computer experience. So search is the next major feature of Tiger, the most important breakthrough feature. And we call it Spotlight. And Spotlight is going to make a lot of things we need to do every day really easy. Like, for example, coming over here, I probably need to get a hold of all the documents that are being created for coming to the Apple Expo. It doesn't matter what kind of application they were used or where they come from, what directories they're in. I just need to find them all and manage them. Or maybe something detailed, like I want to keep track of all the 1200 DPI CMYK images that Ken sent to me. I should be able to do that on my computer.

Or something as broad as I just want to track everything on my computer about Bertrand. I want to know his contact information, email messages we've exchanged, meetings we have coming up. I want that all to work together. Well, Spotlight does that, and it does it in a way that's just super fast, just like iTunes. And it's automatic. It works with standard file formats, like MPEGs and JPEGs and MPEG movies and MP3 music files and all the things that you're used to just work within Spotlight. And developers who create new file formats can extend it and make sure they work with Spotlight. It works with your current applications and documents. You don't have to upgrade your apps, you don't have to change your documents. They'll now work with Spotlight.

And it finds both content, the things you have in your document like words you type in a letter, as well as the metadata or information about the document, like who sent it to you or when did you last look at it. So we're building Spotlight into the system. We're building it into work in the Finder, as well as many of the system applications we all use. We're building Spotlight to work with your address book and your preferences and mail and iChat and iCal, make it all work together and make our personal computer experience much better. So let me go over to a system here and give you a demo of Spotlight right now.

So here I am in Mac OS 10 in Tiger. Now, this is the first time we've shown this publicly. So we'll keep our fingers crossed that the demo gods are with us and that everything works as as promised. This is a system that's not only got Tiger on it, it's packed full of files. We've got over 100,000 files on this system. And we'll start just like we're used to working on Mac OS 10 today. I open up my Finder and I have a search field. Well, that's not new and I can type in anything. Like I type in the word toy, and unlike today, instantly files come back. But that's sort of like I'm used to. I see a lot of files that have toy in the name. Well, that's not so advanced. Let me do something different. Let me type in something like Pixar. And now I get instantly more results. Here's over 50 files that showed up when I typed in Pixar. But if you look at those files, I don't see Pixar in the name anywhere. Where did that come from? Well, let me open up one of them. Here's a Finding Nemo trailer and sure enough, it is Finding Nemo.

As I look through it, it's the Finding Nemo trailer, when we get information on this movie, well, look at there, right in the copyright information, it says copyright 2003 Disney and Pixar. Spotlight in the Finder found a file that had Pixar in the copyright information or metadata about that file. It's fast and easy and it's just remarkable on the things it can find in our system. Let me do another search. Let me go in and, for example, in in my daily work, I may be looking for all the files that I have that have anything to do with the iMac. I get a ton of files. Here's 137 back. I want to refine my search further. Now there's a new pane here. I just click the plus button and I can further refine my search. I'm going to choose kind and presentations. Now, I've created a search that finds any presentation file that has anything to do with iMac, whether that's in the contents inside the presentation or in the name or metadata. I see a bunch of both Keynote and PowerPoint files come up. Well, maybe I do this all the time. I'm working on some key some Keynote presentations about iMac. I just click the save button and I call this iMac presentations. Let me save that on my desktop. And now, anytime I want to keep track and look for those files I'm working on on my presentations on the iMac, I just open up that smart folder. And that smart folder will constantly keep track of it all.

Now I have a I have a couple other examples of smart folders here in the desktop just to show you how powerful they are. I have one called files from Ken. This is a folder that notices any file that Ken sends me and keeps track of it, no matter where it goes on my system. So now if Ken and I are working on a project together, I don't have to reorganize all my files. I can just find the ones from Ken and the smart folder will keep track of them for me. Or like the example I mentioned in my slides, here's one called images for print. Let me open up the criteria on that to see what is it finding. It's finding anything that's of the file kind an image. It's got a color space of CMYK, which is what I need for printing, and its resolution is greater than 1200 DPI. So that's finding all my high quality print files that have anything to do with Apple products and images. And it keeps track of them. Again, no matter where they are in my system, they're always managed in my smart folder. So that's smart folders. One of the things that get empowered by Spotlight. I'm going to give you another example of the real power of Spotlight. We knew building it into the Finder would be really useful. And then we thought, well, isn't it great to get access to this no matter what application you're in? So we created a new menu item. You'll see in the top right corner of the menu that blue button and it has a magnifying glass on it. So no matter what application you're in, you just click it and you get a search field. And I can start typing in anything I want and instantly it starts finding those files. So I typed in the word Paris. Maybe I'm coming to Paris and instantly it finds all the files on my system that have anything to do with Paris. Articles, contacts of people in Paris, documents, folders, images, everything I need to do with Paris. Maybe when I'm coming over here, I'm going to visit the Louvre. So we type in the Louvre and instantly again, it finds a whole bunch of documents, contacts. There's a restaurant near the Louvre, images, mail messages about the Louvre, documents. For example, well, here's one, Paris Metro map. Now why did that show up in a Louvre search? It doesn't say Louvre in the title. Let's open it up. It's a PDF file. We'll zoom in a couple times. Now highlighted for you so so you see it right there in the text inside a PDF file, the Louvre.

So you can get access to this this Spotlight menu anytime you're in any application and it gives you the most frequent and and and and the top ranking things that show up for the Louvre, but it has at the first menu item says show all. There's actually 32 items, longer than this list can hold. So I click that and I get the new Spotlight window that helps us manage all these searches if we want even more control over them. For example, not only do I see them organized, contacts, folders, images, I can select how to organize them. That's by kinds. Maybe I want to organize them by date, the latest things. Now, I just opened that Paris Metro map for the Louvre. That now shows up the first thing under today because it keeps track of when I open these things up. Or maybe by the people who sent them to me. So it's something from the Louvre. I know Bertrand sent it to me. I can just organize by person. And I can see a lot of information. For example, see these images? Let me set them into a larger a larger icon view and I can see the images there that have anything to do with the Louvre and I can just click one and open it right from here. So the Spotlight search window gives us tremendous power over managing all the documents in our system.

Well, the last thing I want to show you is how Spotlight starts to work across other applications as well. Not just in the Finder, not just in the Spotlight menu, but all the applications we use. Well, first I'll I'll do one that you wouldn't expect to find Spotlight searching in. But we've really thought hard about how it can help us in our everyday life. So, for example, here it is in the system preferences. Normally you used to go to the system preferences and click on a preference and and dive deep to find what you want. You don't have to do that anymore. Now there's a Spotlight search field. I can just start to type what I want. For example, maybe I want to change my desktop picture. I type picture and it highlights for me where I'm going to find to change my desktop picture. I just select it and I'm taken right to that setting and I can set it myself. Or maybe I'm a Windows user and I'm not up on all the latest Mac lingo yet. Perhaps I might know it better from the Windows world as wallpaper. And sure enough, wallpaper tells me that I'll find that setting in desktop pictures. Or maybe I want to go set my airport settings. I just start to type in airport and it finds it for me. Again, maybe I'm a Windows user and I don't know airport, so I'll type in Wi-Fi. And again, it shows me the choices for setting my Wi-Fi settings. Or 80211. And again, I'm shown where to go to set that setting. So Spotlight can be useful to a lot of the different applications we use. And this really starts to tie together applications in new ways and make them incredibly powerful. For example, I mentioned in my slide the address book. Within the address book, we've also built in Spotlight support. So, for example, just like you have smart folders on the desktop, you can now have smart address books. Here's one example, a smart address book that tells me who has an upcoming birthday. It looks at the birthday field in the address book and if anybody has a birthday coming within 30 days, it dynamically shows up in the smart address book. And I can look at it and wait a minute, I see Bertrand has a birthday coming up in in a few days and and so there's Bertrand and it found his birthday for me and and now you can start to see how Spotlight makes all these applications work together. There's a new choice where if I can click on Bertrand's name, it says perform a search with Spotlight on this person. And up pops my Spotlight search window and it shows me instant messaging.

It shows me instant messaging chats I've had with Bertrand, his contact information, documents Bertrand sends me. He sent me a Unix technology overview. He and I are talking a great deal about the the merits of different corn shells in the Unix environment. And we have events coming up. I can see there's a Bertrand's birthday is an event. That's good because I don't want to miss his birthday. So when I click on it, I'm taken right to the iCal event that shows me, yes, I kept track of Bertrand's birthday on my calendar and I won't forget it. So Spotlight ties together all these applications in one environment where now you can keep track of whatever you wish. So that's a quick glimpse of Spotlight, the most innovative feature coming in Mac OS 10.

And I hope with that just a few minutes of demonstration, you see why we're so excited about how Spotlight is going to change how we work with a personal computer and make our lives just so much more pleasurable. All right, now let's talk about rich media, something the Mac is also known for. We've always been at the cutting edge of the the latest and greatest audio and video formats and open standards. And there's a new one coming. If you haven't heard about it, this is really exciting. It's called H.264. Not the easiest to remember name, but it comes from the MPEG committee, the same people that brought us MPEG 2 for DVDs or MPEG 4 for the the greatest format so far for streaming on the internet and it's been adopted by 3G cell phone makers. Well, H.264 is the next great video standard from MPEG and it's been ratified for as a standard for the next generation high definition DVDs. So as we all start to buy HD DVD players and HD DVDs, they'll be supporting this new H.264 codec that will already be built into your Mac and supported in QuickTime. It's incredible high quality, super efficient codec. And really it's the first one that scales from small high performance sizes like what's needed for cell phones up to true cinematic experiences with HD content. So I said it's a ratified industry standard and it's non proprietary and open, which we really believe is the way to go with these formats. And it's built into the next QuickTime that will come in Mac OS 10. So we can have experiences that are super efficient in streaming video over the internet or incredible high quality HD video experiences. I'd like to invite Ken Bereskin up, senior director of product marketing for Mac OS 10 to show us H.264. Ken?

Thanks, Ken. See, hopefully you see why we're excited about H.264, the incredible video quality we're all going to have access to on our systems and the applications that people build that use QuickTime on those computers. Next up, Safari. Safari is a great browser. In fact, the best browser that's ever been on the Mac platform. It's the fastest browser, the best support for open standards. And in Tiger, we integrate a brand new emerging standard into Safari ahead of any other platform. It's called Safari RSS. RSS stands for really simple syndication. Well, why do we need another format or technology for the internet? HTML is great for viewing web pages. But what if you want to track the latest information on something you care about, your sports team, your favorite products? You want to just track some exciting things. How do you do it? Well, with RSS, you get data streams that let you track that news in entirely new ways. You may not know it, but many of the websites you visit today already support RSS streams, places like Yahoo, BBC, Spiegel, New York Times have RSS feeds. You just haven't had a great way to explore those and take advantage of those. Well, we're doing something no one's done before. We're integrating RSS into Safari, into the browser using industry standard protocols. And we're making it really easy because when you go to a website, it will autodetect whether there's RSS support on that website for you. And with the power of RSS in Safari, you can create your own personal clipping services. It's like making your own newspaper. You pick the sites you want to get news from, what topic you want to have covered and you can save those automatically.

in your bookmarks bar, and every day just check the news you're interested in across many different sites all together in one simple page that you create.

So let me show you how Safari works with RSS.

So again, we go back to our Mac OS 10 Tiger system, and we launch Safari with its RSS support.

And it looks like the Safari we all know and love.

But now I can go to different sites, for example, Liberation.

And you'll see that not only am I visiting this HTML web page, but I see this RSS button now in the address bar. And if I click on it, I get that website in an RSS feed. You see how that now gives me a data feed of all the news in a simple, quick, easy to view format. And I can control it. I can, for example, decide how long I want the articles to be and whether I just want to see the titles, so I can get a quicker view or or spread it out. And I can sort by date or title or source, and I can view what's to all the news or just what's from today or yesterday. So I get great control over what my viewing experience is.

Here's another site, BBC Entertainment. Again, I'm looking at it as a standard HTML as we do today, but it's also an RSS feed. I see that button again. Let me click on the RSS feed, and I get the BBC Entertainment site now as an RSS feed, and I can look at it in many different ways, and I can just click on any story I want to go to.

Oh, there's a lot of interesting news today up there.

Willis fined for clearing islands. And you can jump right to any HTML feed you want right from that RSS feed. But the real power comes when you start looking across multiple sites. That's when RSS really really screams for us. So, for example, I'm going to click on this one button that says Tech. It actually is seven different websites that all have RSS feeds. What I'm seeing is data from SciTech, BBC News, CBS MarketWatch, CNET, E-Week, Wired, and Yahoo, all together in this one page designed for me. As you see, there's over 600 new stories, four four brand new since the last time I visited this page. Well, I can further refine my search. Maybe I'll type in Apple.
